title: AHPRA Information Session for Overseas-Trained Nurses
description: Free information session for nurses qualified overseas who want to register to practise in Australia. Covers the AHPRA assessment pathway, OSCE preparation, bridging programs at RMIT and Holmesglen TAFE, English requirements (OET vs IELTS), and document checklists. Run by Royal Melbourne Hospital nursing educators with mentors from the local African and South Asian communities. Tigrinya, Amharic, Arabic, Hindi, and Punjabi interpreters on hand. Bring your transcripts if you want a quick eligibility check after the session.
organizer: Royal Melbourne Hospital + City of Melbourne Libraries
audience_notes: Aimed at overseas-trained nurses preparing for AHPRA OSCE. Children welcome; no childcare provided.

title: Engineers Australia CDR Workshop for Migrant Engineers
description: Hands-on workshop for overseas-qualified engineers preparing a Competency Demonstration Report (CDR) for Engineers Australia migrant skill assessment. Walk through career episode structure, summary statement, CPD log, and common rejection reasons. Run by Engineers Australia migrant mentors who have personally guided 50+ engineers through CDR. Farsi, Dari, and Arabic interpreters available. Bring a laptop and a draft CV.
organizer: Migrant Workers Centre + Engineers Australia (Victoria Division)
audience_notes: Open to any engineering discipline (civil, structural, electrical, mechanical, chemical, software). Beginners welcome.

title: Kensington Saturday Homework Club
description: Free weekly drop-in homework club for kids from Prep to Year 10. Volunteer teachers and university students help with maths, English, science, and any school assignments. Hosted by a Kensington Primary teacher. Parents welcome to stay, drink tea, and ask questions about navigating the Victorian school system. Vietnamese and English spoken. Most kids in the room have at least one migrant parent.
organizer: Kensington Primary parents + City of Melbourne Libraries
audience_notes: Kids Prep–Year 10. Drop-in, no registration. Parents stay or leave kids supervised by volunteers.

title: Kensington Eid al-Adha Community Iftar
description: Free community Eid al-Adha celebration hosted by the Sudanese and Eritrean Australian communities at Kensington Town Hall. Traditional Sudanese, Eritrean, and Afghan food; music; kids' activities; and storytelling from elders. Everyone welcome — newcomers, long-time Kensington residents, and friends of the East African and South Asian communities. Arabic, Tigrinya, Amharic, Farsi, and Dari widely spoken; English-speakers warmly welcomed.
organizer: Sudanese Australian Integrated Learning Centre + Eritrean Community Association of Victoria + Hazara Australian Association of Victoria
audience_notes: All ages, all backgrounds. Halal food. Modest dress appreciated. Free face-painting for kids.

title: ESL Conversation Circle
description: Weekly drop-in conversation circle for English language learners at every level. Volunteer facilitators help with everyday English — bus signs, GP appointments, school newsletters, job interview practice. No registration, no test, no judgement. Free tea and biscuits. A great way to meet other newcomers from across the world. Mostly conversational English; volunteers also speak Vietnamese, Tigrinya, Amharic, and Farsi.
audience_notes: Adults. Children welcome but must be supervised. All English levels — true beginners encouraged.

title: African Australian Women's Health Forum
description: Free half-day forum for African Australian women covering preventive health, women's health screening, mental health, and navigating Medicare. Run by African Australian doctors and the Royal Women's Hospital outreach team. Tigrinya, Amharic, Arabic, and Somali interpreters available. Free childcare with bookings; lunch provided. Women only.
organizer: Royal Women's Hospital + African Australian Multicultural Employment & Youth Services (AAMEYS)
audience_notes: Women only. Free childcare available — book at least 5 days ahead.

title: Migrant Maker Market & Skill Swap
description: Monthly market and skill-swap at Flemington Community Centre, just over the rail line from Kensington. Stalls run by migrant makers — handcrafted goods, food, clothing, plants. The 'skill swap' corner is a free notice board where you can post or take up offers — e.g. 'I'll teach Tigrinya in exchange for resume help' or 'I'll cook a homecooked Afghan meal in exchange for tax-return advice'. Genuinely warm, family-friendly, multilingual.
organizer: Flemington Community Centre + local Afghan, Eritrean, and Vietnamese organisations
audience_notes: All ages, all backgrounds. Bring a small thing to swap if you can; not required.

title: Free Tax Help & ABN Workshop for New Arrivals
description: Practical workshop for migrants who have arrived in the past three years. Covers TFN, MyGov, lodging your first tax return, claiming work-related deductions, ABN basics, GST thresholds, and lodging a quarterly BAS. Run pro bono by Vietnamese-Australian and Eritrean-Australian CPAs from the inner west. Vietnamese and Tigrinya interpreters on hand. Bring your TFN, payslips, and any receipts.
organizer: CPA Australia (volunteer chapter) + Kensington Neighbourhood House
audience_notes: Designed for migrants in their first three years in Australia. Limited to 25 attendees.
